record.original_question: Let $B$ be an $n x n$ (upper) bidiagonal matrix. Is there an algorithm that, in $O(kn)$ operations, can produce $k$ triples $(sigma_i,v_i,u_i)$ such that $sigma_i >= 0$, $v_i, u_i C^n$ are unit vectors, and, for machine precision $epsilon$, $ |Bv_i-sigma_iu_i |_2 = O(epsilon n |B |_2)$; $|v_i^Hv_j|$, $|u_i^Hu_j| = O(epsilon n)$ if $i != j$.

evidence.quote: Let $B$ be an $n \times n$ (upper) bidiagonal matrix. Is there an algorithm that, in $O(kn)$ operations, can produce $k$ triples $(\sigma_i,v_i,u_i)$ such that $\sigma_i \geq 0$, $v_i, u_i \in {\mathbb C}^n$ are unit vectors, and, for machine precision $\epsilon$, \begin{enumerate} \item $\|Bv_i-\sigma_iu_i\|_2 = O(\epsilon n\|B\|_2)$; \item $|v_i^Hv_j|$, $|u_i^Hu_j| = O(\epsilon n)$ if $i \neq j$. \end{enumerate}

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$ be an upper bidiagonal matrix (i.e., $B_{ij} = 0$ unless $j = i$ or $j = i+1$), and let $\epsilon > 0$ denote a fixed machine precision. Let $1 \le k \le n$ be an integer. Does there exist an algorithm that, using only $O(kn)$ arithmetic floating-point operations (in a standard model of floating-point arithmetic with unit roundoff $\epsilon$), produces $k$ triples $(\sigma_i, v_i, u_i)$ for $i = 1, \ldots, k$ with $\sigma_i \ge 0$ and $v_i, u_i \in \mathbb{C}^n$ unit vectors (in the Euclidean norm) such that the following hold:

1. (Approximate singular triple) For every $i \in \{1,\ldots,k\}$,
$$\|B v_i - \sigma_i u_i\|_2 = O(\epsilon\, n\, \|B\|_2).$$

2. (Numerical orthogonality) For all $i \ne j$ in $\{1,\ldots,k\}$,
$$|v_i^H v_j| = O(\epsilon\, n), \qquad |u_i^H u_j| = O(\epsilon\, n).$$

Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ denotes the spectral (operator $2$-) norm for matrices and the Euclidean norm for vectors, and $v^H$ denotes the conjugate transpose. The implicit constants in the $O(\cdot)$ bounds must be independent of $B$, $n$, $k$, and $\epsilon$.
artifact.status_search_result: The MRRR (Multiple Relatively Robust Representations) approach has been proposed to compute k singular triples of a bidiagonal matrix in O(kn) time and storage. However, a fully stable, provably correct version of MRRR for the SVD with the required residual and numerical-orthogonality guarantees is not publicly available in standard libraries such as LAPACK; existing implementations (e.g., BDSVDX, based on an associated tridiagonal eigenproblem) do not achieve the O(kn) complexity together with the stated accuracy guarantees. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Computing the Bidiagonal SVD Using Multiple Relatively Robust Representations
status_evidence.snippet: k singular triplets can be computed using only O(nk) storage units and floating point operations.
status_evidence.claim: MRRR aims to compute k bidiagonal singular triples in O(kn) work, but a stable implementation with the required guarantees is still lacking.

status_evidence.title: Bidiagonal SVD Computation via an Associated Tridiagonal Eigenproblem
status_evidence.snippet: BDSVDX computes the SVD of a bidiagonal matrix through the eigenpairs of an associated symmetric tridiagonal matrix, enabling computation of a subset of singular values and vectors.
status_evidence.claim: Current LAPACK routines for partial bidiagonal SVD do not achieve O(kn) complexity with the specified residual and orthogonality bounds.

status_evidence.title: LAPACK Working Note 166: Computing the Bidiagonal SVD Using MRRR
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses challenges in obtaining a numerically stable MRRR for the bidiagonal SVD.
status_evidence.claim: A fully stable MRRR-based bidiagonal SVD with provable O(kn) accuracy guarantees has not been established.
